response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net_fee_rate > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Record count is the number of qualifying fee rows in the group (COUNT(*)), including rows whose rebrate is NULL, even though those rows add nothing to the average net rate.

Rows with a NULL rebrate give a NULL net rate and are ignored by the group average. Groups whose net rates are all NULL have a NULL average, are left out of the side average, and cannot satisfy the strict comparison.
The side average is the unweighted mean of the group averages for that side, not a mean over individual fee rows.
Each orderslink matches at most one order, since recordvault is described as a unique order reference. Ties in the difference are ordered arbitrarily.
